$doc: Tests that are RED on main and are tolerated by scripts/test-ratchet.js until their finding is closed.
This list may only ever SHRINK. The ratchet fails the build if a test not listed here fails (a regression),
and equally if a test listed here starts passing (remove it and close the finding).
Every entry carries the finding id that owns the fix, so nothing here is 'silenced' — it is queued.
Established 2026-08-02 by the Daily Improvement V3 run for S-E02-2 (PF-55 / VAL-01), the first time these
suites had ever been executed. 18 entries at establishment.
SECOND HALF — 'skipped' (TOOL-13, 2026-08-12). A failure list alone cannot notice a test that STOPS
EXECUTING: a skipped test is not a failure, so it left the set, and the ratchet reported '✓ no drift.'
about checks it had not performed. So each app may also carry a 'skipped' block: per suite path, the number
of tests that DID NOT RUN (jest statuses pending / todo / skipped / disabled — a describe.skip surfaces as
'pending', not 'skipped').
The counts may only ever FALL. A RISE fails the gate exactly the way a new failure does — it means fewer
tests executed than this file records. A suite recorded here but ABSENT from the run fails too: the suite
stopped existing. A FALL does NOT fail: it is usually someone un-skipping a test, and reddening the gate on
them would get the gate routed around within a week — it is reported instead, loudly, because a fall is also
what a DELETED test looks like, so check before you run --update.
Only non-zero counts are recorded. The residual is stated rather than hidden: a suite with no entry here that
vanishes entirely is not caught by this half — that needs a full suite inventory, which is a follow-on.
An app with no 'skipped' block at all is not an error: the ratchet prints an unmissable INACTIVE warning and
qualifies its verdict line, so a half-performed check can never read as an unqualified green. Populate it with
`node scripts/test-ratchet.js <app> --update` from a COMPLETE run — --update and --skip stay mutually
exclusive, now for two reasons: a partial run drops the failures it did not see AND writes the counts of the
unrun suites as absent.
